To rerun a failed or flaky build on a PR, comment `retest this please` on the PR; Jenkins picks it up within a minute.","criticality":0.5,"epistemic":"fact","id":"01a10827-7d90-7292-b752-2105f7b21874","invalidated_at":"2026-10-04T18:22:51.974025356Z","logical":["ci"],"physical":["/"],"provenance":"human","status":"challenged","summary":"Rerunning CI builds","superseded_by":"01a10827-8ae0-74a2-a635-ee95522abf0f","tags":["ci","workflow"],"type":"convention","visibility":"shared"}}

CI runs on **Buildkite** now, since Jenkins was shut down on 2026-08-12. You can rerun the failed build in either of two ways:

- **In the Buildkite UI:** click through from the failed check on your PR to the build and press **Retry** on the failed job. This reruns only that job, not the whole pipeline.
- **From the command line:** run `bk build retry <build-number>`, using the build number shown in the PR check.

Don't comment `retest this please` on the PR. That only worked with Jenkins and does nothing now.

A team note still described the old Jenkins method, so I've marked it as outdated and pointed it to the current Buildkite note. This information comes from those team notes; there's no CI config in the repo to check it against.

If the same test keeps failing, it may be worth fixing. To check whether it fails locally too, run `make test-fast` a few times.
